hypotheses.justification: The statement only mentions `ModularCurve.smoothedFundamental Γ T`. It is defined for any subgroup as `∑ᶠ q : SL(2,ℤ) ⧸ Γ, puCut T (mob q.out z)`, so finite index is not needed for the statement to elaborate. The proof uses finite index only through `carrier`/`mem_carrier_of_ne_zero` (via `smoothedFundamental_eq_sum`, which needs `[Fintype (SL(2,ℤ) ⧸ Γ)]`). Proof without it: let S = {δ : SL(2,ℤ) | δ•{τ} meets boxH T}; S is finite by `finite_moving {τ} (boxH T) isCompact_singleton (isCompact_boxH T)`, which needs no finite index. If smoothedFundamental Γ T (γ•τ) ≠ 0, the finsum is nonzero. Its support is then finite (`finsum_of_infinite_support`, the additive form of `finprod_of_infinite_mulSupport`), so some term is nonzero: puCut T (mob q.out (γ•τ)) ≠ 0. By `mob_mob`/`coe_smul` this is puCut T (mob (q.out*γ) τ) ≠ 0. The argument of `mem_piece_of_ne_zero` then gives (q.out*γ)•τ ∈ boxH T, i.e. q.out*γ ∈ S. Since γ ∈ Γ, q is the coset of δ := q.out*γ and γ = q.out⁻¹*δ (injectivity of `cosetEquiv`). So the support lies in the preimage under the injective Subtype.val of the image of the finite set S under δ ↦ (↑δ : SL(2,ℤ)⧸Γ).out⁻¹*δ, and is finite. Degenerate case: when the index is infinite, a finsum with infinite support is 0 by convention, which only shrinks the support.
